GET /seat/search 를 추가한다.

기존 좌석 조회는 본인 좌석 또는 좌석별 예약 가능 여부 boolean뿐이라
특정 전화번호가 어느 좌석을 예매했는지 확인할 수단이 없었다.

- UserRepository.findByPhoneNumber + SeatReservationRepository.findAllByUserId
  조합으로 처리해 신규 레포지토리 메서드와 QueryDSL 쿼리는 추가하지 않는다
- 응답은 기존 GetSeatResponse 재사용, PERFORMER의 다중 좌석을 위해 배열로 반환
- 유저가 없으면 404 USER_NOT_FOUND, 예매 좌석이 없으면 빈 배열
- SecurityConfig 매처는 선언 순서상 GET /seat 위에 배치

Use the font cache of openhtmltopdf instead of our own font resolver
CachingJava2DFontResolver stopped the leak of Font.createFont() for @font-face
fonts, but it broke the fonts of the documents rendered to PNG:

- the @font-face rules are imported by Java2DRenderer when it is built, and
  the resolver was replaced after that, so the new one never got them and the
  fonts of the document were not found (system fonts were used instead)
- it mapped one Font per family name, so a family declared with several
  weights and styles (@font-face in various weights) used the same font for all

openhtmltopdf has a font cache since 1.1.87, which keeps the descriptors with
their weight and style and caches the fonts of the @font-face rules in a cache
shared by all the renders: use it with Java2DRendererBuilder.cacheFonts(true).

CachingJava2DFontResolver stopped the leak of Font.createFont() for @font-face
fonts, but it broke the fonts of the documents rendered to PNG:

- the @font-face rules are imported by Java2DRenderer when it is built, and
  the resolver was replaced after that, so the new one never got them and the
  fonts of the document were not found (system fonts were used instead)
- it mapped one Font per family name, so a family declared with several
  weights and styles (@font-face in various weights) used the same font for all

openhtmltopdf has a font cache since 1.1.87, which keeps the descriptors with
their weight and style and caches the fonts of the @font-face rules in a cache
shared by all the renders: use it with Java2DRendererBuilder.cacheFonts(true).

Fix remaining memory leak: explicitly clean up ThreadCtx after rendering
In GraalVM native image, ThreadCtx.cleanup() called inside
Java2DRenderer.close() does not fully release the ThreadLocal value.
Each worker thread retains the SharedContext and its entire object
graph (DOM, CSS, layout tree, BufferedImages) from its last render,
leaking ~5-15 MB per thread until OOM.

is always called, even on exception.

[BUILD] distributed-webadmin-integration-tests: reset RestAssured after each test
Three classes set the static RestAssured.requestSpecification (with a
webadmin base path) and never reset it. James's JVM-wide
JMAPTestingConstants.jmapRequestSpecBuilder copies the static spec when it
is first created, so if it is first used right after one of these classes
in the same JVM, every later JMAP request inherits the webadmin base path
and gets a 404.

The current class order in a single fork hides it; any other order (a
different surefire run order, or tests spread over several forks) exposes
it: DistributedTeamMailboxDeletedMessageVaultIntegrationTest followed by
TMailDistributedDeletedMessageVaultIntegrationTest in one JVM fails 7 of 17
tests with 404 before this change, 0 after. Same reset the other contracts
already do.

draw()/dispatchDraw() capturing flag cannot exclude the overlay from a hardware capture

RenderNode reference instead, taking the backdrop blur with it. Neither arrangement both
draws the panel and blurs behind it, so there is no downscale or tuning that rescues it.

Support client-side bloom filter blobs for bloom_match (#1982)
* Support client-side bloom filter blobs for bloom_match

Adds BloomFilterUtils, which builds the MBF1-wrapped Parquet Split-Block
Bloom Filter blob that a bloom_match(field, {blob}) filter expression
consumes. Building the filter on the client and shipping the compact blob
lets large membership sets pass the proxy gRPC receive limit, which a raw
value list would exceed for the same set.

The blob is byte-identical to the ones the Go SDK (client/sbbf) and
pymilvus (build_bloom_filter) produce, so the shared golden vectors are
copied in as test fixtures and compared as full hex -- that is the real
interop check against the server, which never rebuilds the filter.

XXH64 is hand-written rather than pulled in as a dependency: sdk-core has
no XXH64 on its classpath (Guava's Hashing offers murmur3/sipHash/farmHash
but not XXH64, and parquet-column's copy is a sdk-bulkwriter dependency
behind hadoop).

perf(types): обрыв по считающемуся телу не запускает уточняющих проходов
Обрыв входа в метод, тело которого считают круги по ячейкам, ставил тот же
признак, что обрыв цикла, а он запускает уточняющий проход у каждого метода
выше по цепочке. Уточнение подставляет приближение методу из visited, а у
такого метода приближения нет ни у кого: его значение сейчас никто не
считает. Вызывающие же пересчитывались в свежем контексте, заново проходя те
же круги по ячейкам и упираясь в тот же обрыв, - каскадом.

Теперь такой обрыв отдельный: результат он из кэша исключает так же, но
уточнений не запускает. Проверка visited идёт первой, поэтому прямая
рекурсия значения по-прежнему обрывается как цикл, с уточнением.

индексе окончательным - пустым оставался и его вызывающий.

fix(types): член резолвится под унарной операцией
Поиск узла dereference в дереве выражения спускался только под бинарные
операции и аргументы вызова метода. Если обращение к члену стоит под
унарной операцией, корень дерева — унарный узел, и член не находился
вовсе: `Объект.Ссылка.Пустая()` резолвится, а `НЕ Объект.Ссылка.Пустая()`
уже нет.

Видно это было по всем потребителям общего пути `memberAt`: подсветка
семантическими токенами под `НЕ` пропадала и у свойств, и у методов,
молчали hover, переход к определению и поиск ссылок. Громче всех
проявилась диагностика UnknownMember: не найдя член, она добирала тип
получателя запасным путём (по завершающему идентификатору через индекс
ссылок), получала вполне конкретный тип — и объявляла существующий член
неизвестным.

Обход теперь покрывает все виды узлов: унарную операцию, тернарный
оператор и вызовы вообще (раньше — только MethodCallNode, аргументы

fix(binding): pin thread context classloader during context startup
When BSL LS is embedded in a host that isolates the thread context classloader
(e.g. a SonarQube scanner IsolatedClassloader), micrometer's ContextRegistry
static initializer discovers its ThreadLocalAccessor SPI via ServiceLoader on the
context classloader. That happens while the context-propagating task decorator
bean is built during startup, and under an isolating TCCL it cannot see the
ThreadLocalAccessor implementations bundled with this library, so context boot
fails with ClassNotFoundException: io.micrometer.context.ThreadLocalAccessor.

Pin the context classloader to this library's own classloader for the duration
of the boot so the SPI resolves. ContextRegistry initializes once and is cached,
so later usage on the embedder's threads is unaffected. Standalone behaviour is
unchanged. This lets embedders drop their own equivalent workaround.

fix(aop): keep EventPublisherAspect registration eager under lazy-init
EventPublisherAspectRegistration does its work purely as a side effect in
setApplicationContext and is injected by nobody. Under global
spring.main.lazy-initialization=true (used, for example, when embedding via
BSLLSBinding) it was therefore never instantiated: the aspect had no
registered context and dropped every event ("Trying to send event in not
active event publisher"). As a result the document-lifecycle-clearable
indexes (notably InferredExpressionTypeIndex, keyed by ParseTree nodes)
never received their clear events and never evicted, retaining the parse
trees of every analyzed file and causing OutOfMemoryError on large scans.

Force the registrar eager with @Lazy(false), matching how the aspects
themselves are already declared in AspectJConfiguration.

perf(references): avoid throwaway Range in terminal ReferenceFinder lookup
The default ReferenceFinder.findReference(uri, TerminalNode) computed the
terminal's start position via Ranges.create(terminal).getStart(), allocating a
Range (two Position objects) only to keep one and discard the rest. The
non-overriding finders include the hottest one (ReferenceIndexReferenceFinder),
so every source-symbol terminal lookup allocated on that path — in a workspace
whose heap is already dominated by Position/Range objects (issue #4248).

Add a small Positions utility (mirroring Ranges) that builds a bare Position
from a Token/TerminalNode — the token->LSP-position conversion (line - 1,
charPositionInLine) previously inlined in several places — and use it in the
default overload. Result is identical to the previous start position (covered
by PositionsTest parity assertions against Ranges.create(...).getStart()).

perf(diagnostics): skip descent into non-compound statements in EmptyStatement
EmptyStatementDiagnostic.visitStatement descended into every statement's full

nested empty statements. Result is identical (8 diagnostics on the SSL module

fix(context): require exact selection-range match in declaration lookup
The selection-range lookup in getMethodSymbol(ctx)/getVariableSymbol(ctx)
returned any symbol whose selectionRange merely *contained* the start of the
computed range. The previous linear scan required exact range equality and
so returned empty for non-declaration or error contexts (e.g. callers that
pass ctx.getParent() or a broken node whose start falls inside a neighbouring
symbol's name). Without that guard an extra symbol was resolved — surfacing
as CognitiveComplexityCodeLensSupplierTest seeing 3 code lenses instead of 2.

the performance win while restoring the prior semantics.

fix(cli): guard against accidental Spring Boot debug mode
Passing --debug/--trace or setting the DEBUG/TRACE environment variables
(Spring binds them to the debug/trace properties via relaxed binding) turns
on verbose core-logger logging plus the auto-configuration report. Over LSP
stdio that stray output can corrupt the protocol channel, and DEBUG is a
common env var that is easy to set by accident.

Spring Boot does not let you rename or disable the debug/trace keys, so guard
them before the context boots: honor the request only when the explicit
--enable-debug-i-know-what-i-am-doing opt-in is given on the command line.
Otherwise strip the flags from the args and force debug/trace to false via
system properties (higher precedence than env vars), warning on stderr.

Имя класса/модуля выводится из имени файла, а на macOS файловая система
хранит имена в форме NFD (например, «й» = «и» + U+0306). Идентификаторы в
исходном коде (и в «Новый ИмяКласса») набираются в NFC. Без нормализации
имя из файла МойКласс.os (NFD) не совпадало с МойКласс в коде (NFC), и
автодополнение/hover/переход к определению по классу из такой библиотеки
не работали.

OScriptLibraryIndex теперь нормализует qualifiedName к NFC при регистрации
(имя попадает в TypeRegistry и в completion-метки) и приводит ключ поиска
к NFC+lower-case (nameKey). Аналогично нормализуется basename для не
библиотечных .os в OScriptModuleMembersProvider.

fix(oscript): автокомплит библиотечного класса при #Использовать "путь"
Класс из каталога-библиотеки, подключаемого относительным путём
(#Использовать "lib"), не попадал в автокомплит, когда рядом с
потребляющим скриптом (плоский .os в корне workspace) лежит сам каталог
библиотеки.

Причины:
1. ConventionalLibraryDiscovery при обнаружении плоских .os в корне
   workspace регистрировал его как flat-библиотеку и прекращал обход — в
   результате каталог-библиотека lib/ не индексировался как отдельная
   библиотека (класс попадал лишь как implicit-запись с libOrigin корня).
   Теперь на корневом уровне обход продолжается, и lib/ индексируется как
   полноценная convention-библиотека (libOrigin = "lib").
2. UseDirectiveScanner учитывал только идентификаторную форму
   (#Использовать имя) и игнорировал строковую (#Использовать "путь").
   Теперь строковая форма распознаётся: для gating'а берётся последний
   сегмент пути (совпадает с libOrigin = имя каталога).

feat(index): индексировать символы по началам CamelCase-слов для префиксного fuzzy
Записи WorkspaceSymbolIndex кладутся в PatriciaTrie не только под полным
lowercase-именем, но и под суффиксами от начала каждого CamelCase-слова
(splitByCharacterTypeCamelCase, кириллица режется корректно): для
«ПровестиДокумент» ключи «провестидокумент» и «документ». Так prefixMap
ловит запрос «слово из середины» (например «Документ») через дерево как
word-start, а не только сканом-подпоследовательностью.

Скоринг: точное < префикс полного имени < префикс слова (word-start) <
подстрока < подпоследовательность. Поиск дедуплицирует запись по
идентичности с лучшим скором (одна запись лежит под несколькими ключами).
clear(uri) удаляет запись из ВСЕХ её ключей (пересчёт keysOf по имени).
fuzzy-добор и пустой запрос идут по уникальным записям indexedByUri, а не
по раздутому дереву; indexedByUri и trie держатся согласованными под одним
write-lock.

Ограничения (честно): word-start trie покрывает префикс полног

perf(types): lock-free бин-индекс желудей (неизменяемый снимок)
resolve вызывается из диагностик в parallel-стримах (по файлам и по
диагностикам), поэтому synchronized сериализовал бы все эти потоки на одном
мониторе. Индекс переведён на неизменяемый Snapshot за
AtomicReference<CompletableFuture<Snapshot>>:

- чтение (resolve) полностью lock-free и параллельно;
- ленивая сборка выполняется ровно один раз — гонщики ждут общий future
  (без дублирующих полных сканов библиотек);
- правки/удаления применяются copy-on-write через CAS;
- правка .os-класса-определения аннотации и переиндексация библиотек
  сбрасывают ссылку (ленивый ребилд), .bsl и события до построения —
  no-op без блокировки.

Явная синхронизация (synchronized) убрана полностью.

The 2nd argument of Колонки.Добавить(name, types, ...) is, by platform
signature, a ОписаниеТипов object. Use the inferencer to detect that

common: Multiplex virtual-thread polling onto a shared poller thread
VirtualThreadPollerNaive occupies a platform thread per waiting file
descriptor, taken from a bounded pool. With >= pool-size interdependent
waiters, the fd that would release them is never polled: deadlock
(Java <= 24 masked this on 1-2 CPUs via CompletableFuture's
thread-per-task fallback for a parallelism-1 commonPool).

Add VirtualThreadPollerShared (default): virtual threads register
(fd, ops, thread) and park; a single platform thread polls all fds plus
a wakeup pipe and unparks ready threads. ~3x throughput at 16+
connections, constant platform thread count. The naive poller remains
available via -Dorg.newsclub.net.unix.VirtualThreadPoller.naive=true and
now uses ForkJoinPool.managedBlock so it cannot starve either.

Accept events sent before the simulation starts and remove the workarounds spread across classes (PR #615)
Events sent before the start are held by the simulation and added to the
future queue right after the entities start, in the order they were sent,
keeping their time. So events at time 0 are processed at time 0, after
the entities' own start events. Events sent after the simulation stops
(finished, terminated or aborted) are rejected with a warning, both when
sent by entities and directly to the simulation. SIMULATION_END is still
accepted so entities can shut down.

The rule lives in CloudSim.trySend()/trySendFirst(), used by
Simulation.send()/sendFirst() and CloudSimEntity.schedule()/scheduleFirst().
The "has ever started" state is a private CloudSim.everStarted field.
No public method was added for it, since Simulation.hasStarted() would
mean the opposite of Startable.hasStarted() after the stop (see #616).

Fixes #581: Cloudlets waiting for packets don't hold their PEs (PR #585)
With CloudletSchedulerSpaceShared, a NetworkCloudlet waiting for packets
kept its PEs. If the sender was in the same VM and waiting for PEs,
neither could run (deadlock).

The PEs of Cloudlets waiting for packets are no longer counted as used,
so Cloudlets in the waiting list (such as the sender) can run. The
number of used PEs is already computed in the loop that updates the
Cloudlets, so this adds no extra loop, collection or event. It only
applies when the VM has a CloudletTaskScheduler (network simulations).

When a Cloudlet receives its packets and there are no free PEs, the
allocation is limited to the VM PEs and the running Cloudlets share the
VM MIPS until some of them finish.

Fixes #147: Add a timeout for CloudletReceiveTask
A CloudletReceiveTask waiting for packets that were never sent kept
its Cloudlet waiting forever, so the simulation never finished.

- CloudletReceiveTask has an optional timeout (in seconds), counted from
  the time the task starts. Zero (the default) keeps the current
  behaviour: the task waits forever.
- When the timeout is reached, the task finishes, isTimedOut() returns
  true and the Cloudlet moves to its next task. A warning is logged.
- Without a timeout, a warning is logged when a task waits longer than
  CloudletReceiveTask.WAIT_WARNING_TIME (60 seconds). It's logged just
  for the first task in each VM, using a single flag, so it adds no
  collection to the scheduler.
- CloudletTaskScheduler.getNextTaskUpdateDelay() is used by the
  CloudletScheduler to schedule the next processing update, so the
  timeout and the warning happen on time and not only at the next event.

Postpone VM creation while Hosts are being powered on (PR #578)
When no Host is powered on in any available Datacenter, but some are
being powered on (due to a startup delay), the broker now logs a single
warning and registers itself in the Datacenters with Hosts powering on.
When one of them powers a Host on, it sends a VM_CREATE_RETRY to the
waiting brokers (after minTimeBetweenEvents), so they create their
waiting VMs. That doesn't count as a VM creation retry.

Before, VM creation failed with one warning per VM and, depending on
the retry settings, VMs were placed only after the retry delay or
moved to the failed list.

If no Host is powered on and none is being powered on, the previous
flow is kept, since the VmAllocationPolicy may power Hosts on as needed.

All checks are O(number of Datacenters): no Host list is scanned.

  Datacenter.addBrokerWaitingHostPowerOn(DatacenterBroker)

Fixes #537: DAG simulation with NetworkCloudlets gets stuck (PR #560)
A CloudletReceiveTask took every packet sent from its source VM to its
cloudlet, without checking the sender cloudlet or the number of expected
packets. When a cloudlet had multiple parents in the same VM, the first
receive task could take all packets, so the next one waited forever.

- CloudletReceiveTask can now be created with the sender cloudlet and
  decides which packets it accepts (isPacketExpected).
- CloudletTaskSchedulerSimple delivers to a receive task just the packets
  it still needs, keeping the remaining ones for other tasks.
  This avoids the hang even when the sender cloudlet is not given.
- Javadoc explains that, without the sender cloudlet, a receive task may
  get packets from another cloudlet in the same VM, and that the
  simulation still hangs if fewer packets are sent than expected
  (no receive timeout yet, see #147).

consider binary media types when describing an entity; fixes #1236
Enunciate had no notion of a media type whose payload is opaque bytes, so a
resource method that produces (or consumes) `application/octet-stream` was
described as `"type" : "string"` with no format at all, rather than as
OpenAPI's `"type" : "string", "format" : "binary"`.

Binary-ness is now inferred from the media type itself: "application/octet-stream",
"application/pdf" and the "image", "audio", "video" and "font" types (among
others) are binary, while a structured syntax suffix such as "+json" or "+xml"
is not, and neither is a wildcard, since nothing can be assumed about the
payload it ends up carrying. The inference can be overridden per media type
with the new "media-types" element of the configuration, e.g.

  <media-types>
    <media-type name="application/vnd.mycompany.thing"/>
    <media-type name="application/octet-stream" binary="false"/>
  </media-types>

fix: method-level @RolesAllowed overrides class-level in security role docs
Per Jakarta Annotations 2.1 spec §3.11: "If applied at both the class
and method level, the method value overrides the class value."

getSecurityRoles() was always merging the parent (class-level) roles
into the method result, even when the method carried its own @RolesAllowed
annotation. This caused generated documentation to show the union of
class-level and method-level roles instead of only the effective roles.

Fix: return early when a method-level annotation is present, matching
the override semantics defined by the spec and enforced at runtime by
JAX-RS and Spring containers.

Affects both the jaxrs and spring-web modules.

Keep the setup wizard closed when a configured database is unreachable (#6333)
* Keep the setup wizard closed when a configured database is unreachable

DatabaseDetective.isDatabaseEmpty caught any connection failure and
reported the database as empty. Both callers, Listener startup and
InitializationFilter, use that result to decide whether to present the
unauthenticated setup wizard, so a database-connectivity failure on an
already-configured deployment reopened the wizard, exposing the stored
database credentials in the rendered form and letting an unauthenticated
user reconfigure and persist their own settings.

Only a genuinely unconfigured instance (no connection URL) is now treated
as empty on a connection failure; a configured instance that cannot be
reached is reported as not empty, so it fails startup with a connection
error instead of reopening setup. Also stop the finally block from
returning inside a close() failure, which could otherwise flip a
non-empty result to empty.

UpdateFilter.authenticatedSuccessfully was an instance field on the
singleton filter, so once any super user authenticated at the first step
of the database-update wizard the flag stayed true for everyone. A
concurrent unauthenticated request could then POST straight to the
review-changes step and run the pending database updates on the strength
of another user's login.

Move the authenticated flag into the HttpSession so each session must
authenticate for itself. The shared update-in-progress state is left
global on purpose so multiple super users can still watch one running
update. Updates the E2E helpers to session scope, makes resetRequest carry
the session forward (a follow-up request is the same client), and adds a
regression test that a second session cannot reuse another session's
authentication.

Use PipeParser for inbound HL7 to remove XML/XXE attack surface (#6223)
The hL7Parser bean was a HAPI GenericParser, which auto-detects message
encoding and routes XML-encoded payloads to HAPI's XML parser. That XML
parser can expose XML external entity (XXE) processing - external file
reads, SSRF and entity-expansion DoS - when its underlying JAXP factory is
not hardened. OpenMRS only ever produces and consumes pipe-delimited (ER7)
HL7v2 messages, so the XML branch is unused attack surface.

Switch the bean to a PipeParser, which rejects XML payloads outright with
an unsupported-encoding error. The HL7ServiceImpl parser field and setter
are widened to the common Parser supertype so injection still resolves and
existing setParser callers remain source-compatible.

Adds a regression test asserting an XML/DOCTYPE/external-entity payload is
refused before any XML processing occurs.

A column key is the client id of the column, while the ColumnMeta is keyed by the
row-less client id sent by the client (the header ids in `_columnOrder`).

ScrollFeature encodes single rows without encoding the header first, so the first
call to getColumns() of the request happens while the table is already positioned
on a row. collectColumns() then looked up the ColumnMeta with keys like
`form:table:5:colId`, never matched, fell back to the declared displayPriority and
dropped the reordered column order.

ScrollFeature now resolves the columns before positioning the table on a row, and
collectColumns() strips the row index before looking up the ColumnMeta so no
row-encoding feature can break the lookup again.

DataTable export: stop lazy exportAll on an empty batch (#15284)
Without a bufferSize, DataTableExporter#exportAll loads data in a loop
until offset reaches LazyDataModel#getRowCount(). If the row count is
larger than the data load() actually returns (e.g. a stale count after
rows were deleted or no longer match the filter, or a model that
over-estimates its count), load() returns an empty list, offset stops
advancing and the loop calls load() with the same offset forever.

This happens inside a normal non-ajax request thread: the CSV is never
written, so the servlet container never notices that the client has
gone away, and the thread keeps hitting the backend until the server is
restarted. Each further click on the export button adds another stuck
thread. The Thread#isInterrupted() check does not help, since request
threads are not interrupted when the client disconnects.

fix #15131: Menu toggleable must keep the server side expanded state (#15251)
`PlainMenu.bindToggleable()` seeds `collapsedIds` from the rendered markup, so
the widget starts from the state the server sent (`p:submenu expanded` or

localStorage held no state it reset `collapsedIds` to `[]` and the following

fix #15240: TextEditor005Test must pass its DataTransfer to Firefox (#15247)
The three copy tests failed on Firefox only, each asserting against an
empty string. The widget is fine: Firefox's ClipboardEventInit declares
only `data` and `dataType`, so the `clipboardData` member handed to the

fix #12885: FilterMeta must not turn an empty collection filter value into null (#15239)
resetToNullIfEmpty nulled empty collections and arrays so that isActive(), which was
filterValue != null, would report the filter as inactive. But the filter value is also
written back into the filter facet, so a UISelectMany bound to an empty collection was
reset to null - and SelectRenderer#isSelected returns true when both the item value and
the component value are null, so an <f:selectItem itemValue="#{null}"/> was rendered as
selected and then written back into the backing bean, turning [] into [null].

Emptiness is now a property of the value, not something encoded by nulling it:
isActive() asks the new isEmpty(), and resetToNullIfEmpty only normalizes blank Strings,
which the default filter input relies on. Simply not nulling, as the issue suggests,
makes an empty collection an active filter and filters everything away.

Apply <labels> when building from a provided Dockerfile
<labels> are only implemented as a LABEL instruction in the Dockerfile that
this plugin generates (DockerAssemblyManager#createDockerFileBuilder, reached
only when isDockerFileMode() is false). With <dockerFile>/<dockerFileDir>/
<contextDir> the user's Dockerfile is used verbatim, so the labels were
silently dropped -- for the classic build as well as for buildx, not only for
buildx as reported.

Pass them explicitly on both paths: buildx gets one --label per entry
(mirroring the neighbouring --build-arg block, no signature change needed),
and the classic build sends them through the new BuildOptions#labels, which
serialises to the Engine API labels parameter like buildArgs already does.

Both are emitted only when labels are configured, so command lines and build
options are unchanged for projects without <labels>. For a generated
Dockerfile the labels are now applied twice with identical values, which is
idempotent.

Standardize checkout-release-branch.sh across all product repos
The script had drifted into five different shapes across the repos: argument required via `${1?…}` or `${1:?…}`, argument plus a `BUILDKITE_BRANCH` fallback, argument with a hand-rolled usage check, the same under a different variable name, and — in one repo — no argument at all, reading `RELEASE_VERSION` from the environment. Having rolled the same one-line fix out thirteen times this week, the divergence is pure friction, so this settles on a single canonical version.

The resolution order is a superset of what every repo did before — argument, then `RELEASE_VERSION` from the environment, then the `release/*` branch the build runs on — so no call site needed changing. The `BUILDKITE_BRANCH` fallback only ever fires on a branch matching `^release/`, and it derives the branch name back from that same value, so it cannot select a branch other than the one the build was already triggered on.

It also closes two latent bugs.

Reset to FETCH_HEAD rather than the remote-tracking ref
`git fetch origin <branch>` always writes `FETCH_HEAD`, but it only updates `refs/remotes/origin/<branch>` when the remote's configured fetch refspec covers that branch. With the default `+refs/heads/*:refs/remotes/origin/*` that Buildkite sets up, the two are equivalent — but on a clone whose refspec was narrowed after `origin/<branch>` already existed, the fetch leaves that ref stale and `reset --hard "origin/$BRANCH_NAME"` silently lands on the old commit: exactly the failure this script is meant to prevent, reintroduced through the back door.

Resetting to `FETCH_HEAD` removes the dependency on the refspec entirely — it is whatever the line above just fetched.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

Realign the release branch on its remote during checkout
`checkout-release-branch.sh` fetched the release branch then checked it out, but never moved the local branch to the fetched commit. Buildkite cleans the working copy between jobs, yet can reuse it — so a `refs/heads/release/x.y` left behind by an earlier job on the same agent survives, and `git checkout` then just switches to that stale local ref instead of the freshly fetched remote one. Anything running afterwards, such as the version bump and the GitHub Release draft created by `finalize_release`, would target the wrong commit.

Adding `git reset --hard "origin/$BRANCH_NAME"` after the checkout makes the branch match the remote unconditionally. `reset --hard` rather than `git pull`: it needs no extra network round trip and cannot produce a merge if the local and remote refs have diverged.

This is the second part of AINFRA-2725, a follow-up to the WooCommerce iOS 25.1 release incident.

fix: make Micrometer metrics opt-in to avoid autoconfig ordering pitfalls
Relying on @ConditionalOnBean(MeterRegistry.class) was unreliable because
Spring Boot does not guarantee a stable autoconfig load order. When this
starter's autoconfig was processed before actuator's
SimpleMetricsExportAutoConfiguration, the condition silently evaluated to
"no MeterRegistry" and the entire metrics module was skipped, leaving
users wondering why no Retrofit metrics showed up after they pulled in
actuator.

Switch to opt-in: retrofit.metrics.enable defaults to false, and users
must set it to true explicitly. The MeterRegistry is then injected
directly, so a missing registry fails fast at startup instead of going

account is backed by, and that definition never changes when the AWS

credentials loader only re-parses accounts whose definition changed,

fix(clouddriver): bound the operation executor and answer 503 with Retry-After when full (#8173)
* fix(clouddriver): bound the operation executor and answer 503 with Retry-After when full

DefaultOrchestrationProcessor ran operations on a pool of up to
Integer.MAX_VALUE threads, so a burst of requests started a thread each
with no backpressure.

The pool is now bounded by clouddriver.operations.executor.max-threads
(default 500) with an optional queue (queue-capacity, default 0). When
every thread is busy, a request that would start a new execution is
refused before the task store is touched and answered 503 with
Retry-After (retry-after-seconds, default 5), which Orca retries. A
repeated request for a task that is already running is still answered.
If another request takes the last thread between the check and the
submit, the task is left FAILED_RETRYABLE so the retry with the same
client request ID runs it.

fix(clouddriver): report an unreachable Redis task store as 503, not 500 (#8110)
When Redis is unreachable for longer than RedisTaskRepository's retry
policy allows, task endpoints such as GET /task/{id} returned HTTP 500.
Orca retries a 503 on any request method but fails the stage on a 500,
so a short Redis blip failed pipeline stages whose operations may still
have been running fine.

Two problems combined:

- ExcessiveRedisFailureRetries had no @ResponseStatus, so kork's
  GenericExceptionHandlers mapped it to 500.
- It was never thrown anyway. It was raised from a Failsafe

  from listeners and rethrows the last failure, so the raw
  JedisConnectionException reached the handler. The retry helpers now
  wrap the exhausted JedisException themselves.

matching how clouddriver's health indicators report an unreachable
dependency.

feat(kubernetes): evaluate health status of custom resources (#8102)
* feat(kubernetes): evaluate health status of custom resources

Custom resources were always reported as stable: the handlers for CRDs
discovered from the cluster, CRDs declared in customResources: and
unregistered kinds all returned Status.defaultStatus().

Add CustomResourceStatusEvaluator, following kstatus conventions:
no status block is stable; a numeric observedGeneration that differs
from metadata.generation is unstable; Stalled=True is failed;
Reconciling=True is unstable; Ready decides stable/unstable; otherwise
status.phase (Failed/Degraded, Pending/Progressing, Paused) is used.
Condition messages are sanitised and truncated.

All three handlers delegate to it. It is off by default behind
kubernetes.customResourceStatus.enabled, so nothing changes until an
operator enables it.

(plans/2026/crd-health-checks.md, PR 1).

fix(kubernetes): retain empty cache entries for kinds with zero live resources (#8054)
When the last live resource of an authoritative kind (e.g. the last
Deployment in a namespace) is deleted, KubernetesCachingAgent's
groupingBy-based resource collection silently drops that kind's key
from the CacheResult instead of reporting it with zero entries.
SqlProviderCache/SqlCache only run their existingIds-minus-currentIds
eviction diff for types present in the CacheResult, so the deleted
resource's cached row was never cleaned up -- it persisted until a
resource of that same kind reappeared in the namespace on a later
cycle, which is what finally triggered the missed eviction as a side
effect.

Backfill a placeholder entry for every kind the agent is authoritative
for so cleanup runs every cycle regardless of live resource count.

KubernetesValidationUtil#validateCredentials short-circuited to valid
before ever checking the account's `namespaces` allow-list. kubectl
still resolved a concrete target under the hood - the kubeconfig
context's default namespace (typically "default") - so requests could
land outside an account's configured namespace restrictions without

fix(front50): repair dormant pipeline staleCheck optimistic-concurrency check (#8022)
Since a 2022 refactor (front50#1142/#1159), the updateTs fingerprint clients
receive on a pipeline could never be echoed back on save: it had no setter,
so Jackson silently dropped it, leaving Pipeline.lastModified always null.
That made the ?staleCheck=true optimistic-concurrency check a no-op for
every caller, including Deck, which has sent staleCheck=true on every save
for years with no effect. SqlStorageService.loadObject (the single-row path
the check reads the stored value from) had a second, independent gap: it
never selected last_modified_at, unlike loadObjects/listObjectVersions.

Add Pipeline.setUpdateTs so the fingerprint round-trips, and populate
lastModified in loadObject. Gate the actual check behind a new
controller.pipeline.save.stale-check-enabled flag, default false, so
existing behavior (check never fires) is unchanged until it's explicitly
turned on for a future release.

Preserve delegate content type for multipart parameters (#3382)
`DelegateWriter` encodes a parameter through the delegate `Encoder` (e.g.
the Jackson encoder), which sets the correct `Content-Type` (such as
`application/json`) on the throwaway `RequestTemplate`. That header was
discarded and `SingleParameterWriter` hard-coded `text/plain`, so JSON
parts of a multipart request were emitted as `text/plain`.

`DelegateWriter` now reads the `Content-Type` produced by the delegate and
passes it through to `SingleParameterWriter.writeWithContentType`, falling
back to `text/plain; charset=<charset>` when the delegate sets no content
type. The previous behaviour for plain single parameters is unchanged.

Fixes #2813

Avoid ClassLoader leak from static default async executor (#3178) (#3394)
* Avoid ClassLoader leak from static default async executor

AsyncFeign held its default ExecutorService in a static singleton
(LazyInitializedExecutorService) that was never shut down. Inside a
servlet container, the daemon thread pool retained a strong reference to
the initial application's ContextClassLoader, so each redeployment leaked
the previous application's ClassLoader and threads, eventually causing a
Metaspace OutOfMemoryError.

Replace the static singleton with an instance-scoped default executor
created per built client, so it (and its threads) become eligible for GC
once the client is discarded. Also add AsyncBuilder.executorService(...)
so callers can supply and own a managed, shut-downable executor.

Fixes #3178

ci: map JDK vendor tokens to JvmVendorSpec constants
The CI matrix passes a short vendor token such as "eclipse" for the test
JDK toolchain. JvmVendorSpec.matching("eclipse") probes the runtime
java.vendor, which Temurin reports inconsistently across versions: JDK 8
reports "Temurin" while 11+ report "Eclipse Adoptium". A plain substring
match therefore cannot resolve a Temurin 8 toolchain, and the same gap
exists for any distribution whose vendor string differs from its token.

Map the known tokens to Gradle's built-in JvmVendorSpec constants, which
recognise every alias a distribution reports, and fall back to a
substring match for anything unmapped. Also guard against a blank vendor
so an empty token no longer narrows the toolchain query.

Mirrors pgjdbc/pgjdbc#4257, which shares this build-logic file.

ci: pass the test JDK vendor to the Gradle toolchain
The per-row post-processing in matrix.mjs read `java_vendor` from

Kafka Connect: Make CommitState.isCommitReady() O(1) (#16453)
This PR addresses the issue mentioned in
https://github.com/apache/iceberg/issues/16361

Previously, each DATA_COMPLETE envelope triggered a re-scan of the
entire readyBuffer to count received partitions, making per-commit
work O(N^2) in the number of buffered messages. Under control-topic
backlog this compounded the backlog and made recovery harder.

The fix: maintain a running receivedPartitionCount that is
incremented in addReady() and reset in endCurrentCommit().
isCommitReady() becomes a constant-time comparison against
expectedPartitionCount.

The change looks simple, but we also verified the edge cases when
the current commit fails and a new start_commit starts, and also
the situation where there are 2 Coordinators running (the previous
Coordinator didn't terminate and comes back as a zombie
coordinator). In both situations, we maintain the same logic before
and after the code change. Added 2 new unit tests to cover t

omits MAP and LIST field IDs (it is designed for column projection, not collision
avoidance). This caused _partition struct child IDs to be reassigned to the same
IDs as MAP/LIST columns, triggering a NPE in PruneColumns.isStruct() during
merge-on-read scans when the _partition metadata column is included in the
projection.

the behavior of the pre-1.11 Spark 3.5 code that this replaced.

sameBlockstate compares each property's value with !=. The values come out of
BlockState.getValues() as boxed Comparable, so this is reference identity. It
is correct for enum and Boolean properties, whose values are singletons, and
for an IntegerProperty it happens to work today because every vanilla integer
property stays inside the -128..127 range the JVM's Integer cache interns
(the largest, age, tops out at 25). Nothing in the comparison guarantees that,
and identity is not what is meant here; equality is.

Objects.equals to match the three other comparisons in this file. Plain
equals would also be correct: both states share one StateDefinition, so the

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Make the shared thread pool's threads daemon so the client can exit
With Baritone installed the client does not exit when the window closes: it
sits in shutdown until Mojang's ClientShutdownWatchdog kills it, about
fifteen seconds later, and on Windows the leftover javaw holds a lock on the
mods folder until then.

The shared pool is built with the default thread factory, so every worker is
non-daemon, and none of them ever exit. The core threads (corePoolSize 4, and
allowCoreThreadTimeOut is never set) park in take() for the life of the JVM
whether or not they have work, and two of them are permanently busy anyway
with CachedWorld's chunk packer and its ten-minute save loop. Once
Minecraft.main returns, those are the only non-daemon threads left.

Daemon threads fix the exit. They also mean a periodic cache save that is
mid-write at exit can be cut off; #5116, which predates this PR, addresses
that with a shutdown hook.

Run finally when a host exception escapes a catch block
A Java exception (e.g. from karate.fail or a host call) or an engine-raised
error thrown inside a catch block propagated straight out of the try
statement, skipping its finally block. Cleanup in finally - such as a
helper that captures a perf event after timing a call - silently never ran.

The escaping exception is now held, the finally block runs, and the
original exception is rethrown unchanged when finally completes normally
(an abrupt finally completion still wins, per JS semantics). Exception
identity is preserved, so failure messages, abort handling and upstream
type checks see exactly what they saw without a finally clause.

Pooled driver quit in a shared-scope call chain frees its slot exactly once
A callee that quit its driver handed nothing up but never released it, and
a caller that quit a callee's driver kept a slot keyed to the callee's
runtime, so the next acquire timed out and the pool stayed exhausted for

reaps quit drivers before creating or while waiting, and treats a release
of an already-freed driver as a no-op. ScenarioRuntime releases a quit
callee driver instead of skipping it, and a caller's quit driver before
adopting a callee's.

fix(js): structuredClone Error message is serialized, not aliased
The Error branch stored the raw `message` value, so a source reference leaked
straight into the clone — `e.message = {x:1}` gave `clone.message === e.message`,
and `e.message = e` broke graph isolation outright.

HTML StructuredSerialize reads `message` only as an own DATA property and stores
its ToString, which sidesteps the problem entirely: the result is a plain string,
so nothing can alias and no cycle is representable. An accessor or absent slot
now leaves the prototype's empty-string default. `message` is excluded from the
own-property copy that follows so an enumerable one cannot clobber the coerced
value.

Error.prototype.toString reads `message` in turn and would recurse without
bound.

fix(js): ASI continuation hint in parse errors; JS-shaped not-a-function messages
A line starting with `[` or `(` continues the previous line when that line has
no `;` — spec ASI, same as Node. The failure then names a token nowhere near
the omitted `;`, and generated code omits semicolons routinely. Parse errors
now append a hint naming the line, the cause and the fix; detection runs only
while the exception is being built, walking back from the failure position.

Precision over recall: the opener must be first on its line, the token before
it must be one that can end an operand, no `;` may sit in between, and an
`if`/`for`/`while`/`switch`/`catch` head is excluded.

`cannot call: [LIT_EXPR] 1` leaked an engine node type where JS says
`1 is not a function`. All three call sites now go through
`JsErrorException.notAFunction`, which names the callee's source text and
carries the same ASI hint when the call's `(` begins a line.

Behavior is unchanged — messages only.

feat(js): Terms gains isPlainObject / isPlainArray / isSymbol for embedders
JsObject, JsArray and JsSymbol are package-private by design, so an embedder
asking "is this engine value a plain object / an array / a symbol" had no
supported answer and resorted to reflection probes or a check-List-first
workaround (a JS array is also ObjectLike). Three public static predicates on
Terms answer it for engine values only — a host java.util.Map, List or POJO is
false for all three.

"Plain" is exact-class, not instanceof: every built-in exotic (JsMap, JsSet,
JsRegex, JsError, JsSymbol, JsFunction) extends JsObject and none but the
functions self-reports, and JsUint8Array extends JsArray — so identity is what
makes plain mean plain. It holds because the interpreter allocates exactly
JsObject for an object literal, Object.create and `new F()` on a plain
constructor, while a constructor derived from a built-in allocates that
built-in's class instead (Interpreter.allocateInstance).

fix(js): run C-style for loops with absent header parts
A C-style for whose test expression was absent (for(;;), for(init;;incr))
never executed its body: Interpreter.evalForStmt had two deliberately-empty
"rare case" branches that skipped the loop machinery entirely. The bug was
wider than the roadmap note said — an absent *init* (for(; test; incr))
also hit the first dead branch, because the branch keyed on the SEMI child
index rather than on which header parts are present.

evalForStmt now detects a C-style header by a top-level SEMI at index 2 or
3, evaluates the init only when present, and locates the condition and
increment relative to the first SEMI (absolute child indices shift when the
init is absent). An absent condition is treated as always-true per spec
14.7.4 — the loop exits only by abrupt completion — in both the
per-iteration let/const path and the shared-binding path; an abrupt
completion pending from the init expression still exits before the body.

fix(match): keep '##(schema)' optional when it is headed for a match
'##(expr)' does double duty. When building data it means "evaluate, inline
the value, drop the key if null". When asserting it is an optional marker -

not be expressed at all, while '##string' and '##number' worked fine.

passed from exactly two places, the match RHS and match header. v2 dropped

fix(core): closing on configure can kill a shared client's in-flight request, and the mock never released
A review disproved by experiment a claim this repository had written down. The
test javadoc said concurrent sharing of one ApacheHttpClient was already broken
and that "closing does not add a new class of failure there". The first half is
true -- request, startTime and currentRequest are per-instance fields every call
overwrites, so the interceptor attaches one request's headers to another's

requests still succeed; closing the transport in apply() kills a request in
flight on another thread outright, SocketException: Socket closed, where the
previous field-nulling let it finish. Reproduced both ways against
httpclient5 5.6.3. That widened the window from a microsecond field race to the
entire duration of every in-flight request.

docs(gatling): design the injector-health check, and say why residue cannot gate it
The parity work established that Karate's per-execution overhead sits between
PerfEvent brackets, so a Gatling report's percentiles are the server's rather
than the client's. That is the good news and the hazard in one fact: an
under-provisioned injector produces a throughput shortfall with clean-looking
latencies, so nothing in the report looks wrong while the system under test is
silently under-loaded.

The note's load-bearing content is which signals may gate. Process CPU load and
heartbeat scheduling jitter measure the machine and can. The per-iteration
residue measures the WORK and cannot: Karate legitimately spends a millisecond
or two per iteration — machine-dependent, 0.6 ms on Apple silicon against
1.8 ms on Graviton3 — so any residue threshold fires on a healthy run. It is
worth reporting, and it is PROFILING.md's unbuilt residue item, but it is not a
gate.

fix(driver): probe timer scheduling in pool liveness check, not just sync eval
The pooled-driver liveness probe (isResponsive) evaluated `1` and returned as
soon as synchronous JS ran. A CPU-starved renderer under a slow CI container can
eval sync JS instantly yet stop firing setTimeout callbacks — the "timer never
fires" degradation that starves page-driven waitUntil conditions. Such a tab
passed the probe and was returned to the pool, poisoning the next scenario.

Probe `new Promise(r => setTimeout(() => r(true), 0))` with awaitPromise so the
check must resolve through the macrotask/timer queue. A stalled timer queue (or a
wedged channel) now trips the bounded 3s timeout and the driver is discarded and
replaced. A microtask would not catch this — it can settle while timers are
starved — so the setTimeout is load-bearing.

http: send HX-Redirect for context.redirect on htmx-originated requests
When a request carries the HX-Request header, context.redirect()
now responds with HX-Redirect: <path> + status 200 instead of a
bare 302 Location. The XHR layer transparently follows 302
redirects and replaces only the configured hx-target swap region —
that strands the document <head> on the previous page (with any
chrome that depends on per-session state: CSRF meta tag, theme
tokens set by an inline script, anything else baked into the
shell). HX-Redirect signals htmx to do a full window navigation,
which re-renders the head with the new session's state.

Non-htmx callers (native form submits, direct GETs) continue to
receive 302 + Location, so the change is purely additive: htmx
gets the swap-friendly form, browsers get the standards-compliant
form. Both context.hasRedirect() and the RedirectException fallback
funnel through a small applyRedirect() helper that branches on
request.isAjax().

http: CsrfProtection.createTemplateToken returns null when no token is available
Previously the template helper always wrapped the result of
getOrCreateToken(session) in a CsrfToken, even when the inner token
was null (no session, or temporary session). The wrapper itself was
truthy, so a template guard like th:if="context.csrf" stayed true
and pages rendered an empty <meta name="csrf-token"> tag for
anonymous visitors. The htmx X-CSRF-Token client wiring then echoed
"null" or empty string back to the server on the first POST after
sign-in.

createTemplateToken now returns null when getOrCreateToken returns
null, so th:if="context.csrf" reads as a clean presence check and
the meta tag is omitted entirely for anonymous renders. Once a real
session exists it returns the wrapper as before.

  wrapper (was assertNotNull on a wrapper holding a null token).

ci: only save NVD cache on success; raise OWASP timeout 120->180min
Same bug fixed in karate-async ci.yml (commit 0fd0ba4): the cache
save was conditional on `always()`, so a run that timed out during
the cold NVD seed would save a partial H2 DB. Subsequent runs would
restore that DB, find a "last_updated" timestamp suggesting freshness,
do a tiny delta update, and silently report zero vulnerabilities for
every dependency.

Evidence in this repo: the 3 nvd-db-* caches were 24-109 MB. A complete
NVD H2 store from a non-truncated cold seed is typically 500MB-1GB.
The 24 MB cache (from a cancelled run on 2026-04-29) was the original
poisoned save; subsequent runs propagated it forward as 109 MB then
108 MB despite each being marked "success".

Fix:
- Save NVD cache only on success() so a failed/cancelled run cannot
  poison the cache for future runs.
- Bump OWASP dependency-check step from 120 -> 180 min so the cold
  seed has enough time to complete (it is what got truncated last
  time)

Switch SessionStore time fields from epoch ms to epoch seconds
Session.created / updated / expires are now epoch seconds (UTC), matching
the legacy karate-core 1.5.0 contract. The post-rewrite implementation
silently regressed to milliseconds, which broke DynamoDB TTL: DDB
interprets the configured TTL attribute as Unix seconds, so a 13-digit
ms value lands ~year 58,200 AD and rows never auto-expire. Affects any
DDB-backed SessionStore (e.g. studio's DynamoDbSessionStore writing the
`expires` attribute to a TTL-enabled table).

InMemorySessionStore + FileSessionStore now use Instant.now().getEpochSecond().
SessionStoreTest gains a new testSessionTimesAreEpochSeconds that asserts
all three time fields are < 1e11 — locks in the contract so a future
regression to ms fails fast.

setter. TEMPLATING.md adds a callout near `sessionExpirySeconds`.

partial NVD database. Combined with the 4h default for
nvdValidForHours, every run risked a full ~347k-record NVD sync that
could exhaust the 45min job-level timeout.

  - Rolling cache key nvd-db-<run_id> with nvd-db- prefix restore so
    each run can persist fresh data while still reusing the most
    recent prior cache.
  - nvdValidForHours=144 (6 days) on the dependency-check step. The
    weekly Saturday cron fires every 168h, so 168 would mean the
    schedule never refreshes; 144 ensures the weekly job always
    triggers a (small) delta sync.
  - Bump job timeout-minutes 45 -> 120 and add a 60min cap on the
    OWASP step, so a cold-cache seed run can complete.

Propagate driver up at scenario exit in shared-scope called features (re #2817)
A multi-scenario called feature deadlocked PooledDriverProvider when the
pool was exhausted: scenario 1 acquired the driver, but the shared-scope
exit branch in ScenarioRuntime.closeDriver returned without releasing or
propagating, so scenario 2 couldn't inherit it and tried to acquire a
fresh one. Propagating to the caller scenario at exit (rather than only
after the whole called feature returns) lets sibling scenarios inherit
through the normal path.

closure-captured var/parameter shared a name with a variable in the
caller's scope, the caller's value won — a dynamic-scope leak breaking

its own `config.url` against the poller's `config` (which had no `url`
key) instead of the factory's captured config. Symptom on 2.0.4:
`config.url` was null; on 2.0.3: the captured `Java.type` wrapper
appeared lost.

Preserve functions when inheriting variables into isolated-scope call (#2805)
When a feature calls another feature with isolated scope (def result = call
read('child.feature')), ScenarioRuntime.shallowCopy wrapped each Map-typed
value in a new LinkedHashMap so the callee couldn't mutate the caller's
state. But JsFunction extends JsObject implements Map, so functions from
karate-config.js (e.g. bar: function(){ ... }) were also getting wrapped,
stripping their callable behavior. The callee then saw bar as a plain map
and failed with 'bar is not a function'.

Add a JavaCallable guard in shallowCopy (same pattern already used in
deepCopy) so functions pass through unmodified.

Fix scenarioName filter leaking into called features (#2804)
When a top-level scenarioName filter is active (IDE 'run single scenario'),
the filter was being applied to every FeatureRuntime — including features
loaded via call read('reusable.feature'). The reusable's anonymous
Scenario: did not match the name, so it was filtered out, no scenarios
ran in the callee, and variables defined in the reusable (via def or
karate.set) were never propagated back to the caller. Full-file runs
were unaffected because no name filter was set.

Move the scenarioName check below the caller != null bypass, matching
the contract already in place for @ignore / @env — user-facing filters
only select top-level scenarios and never exclude scenarios inside
called features.

Parse and evaluate ES6 getters and setters in object literals
Support {get foo() {...}, set foo(v) {...}} in object literals, plus
the contextual-keyword, string-key, and computed-key variants

IDENT is "get" or "set" and the next token starts a property-name
(IDENT/STRING/NUMBER/L_BRACKET). If so, consume the key (or bracketed
key expression) and emit a synthetic FN_EXPR for the body — the same
shape used by shorthand methods. Accessor-keyword detection only
fires contextually: {get}, {get: 1}, {get() {}} continue to work as
a shorthand property, regular key, and shorthand method respectively.

Model: new JsAccessor (package-private) carries the {getter, setter}
pair and is stored as a value in the owning JsObject's map under the
property name. Paired accessors for the same key merge onto one
JsAccessor so {get foo(){}, set foo(v){}} keeps both halves.

Parse and evaluate ES6 computed keys in object literals
Support {[expr]: value} and {[expr]() { ... }} — common in reducers
(`{[action.type]: handler}`), dynamic config builders, and the
destructuring-roundtrip pattern.

Parser: add L_BRACKET to T_OBJECT_ELEM's prefix set; when it is
consumed, parse the bracketed key expression and the closing
R_BRACKET, then fall through to the existing colon/shorthand-method
branches.

Interpreter: evalLitObject recognizes OBJECT_ELEM starting with
L_BRACKET and evaluates the key expression with Terms.TO_STRING
coercion. The after-key position shifts from 1 to 3, and the
shorthand-method / key-value branches use that offset so shorthand
methods with computed keys ({[k]() {...}}) also work.

Destructuring with computed keys ({[k]: newName} patterns) exists in
the spec but is rare; the bindScope path uses the same offsets and

Parse and evaluate ES6 shorthand methods in object literals
Support {foo() { ... }, bar(a, b) { ... }} without the `function`
keyword. Extremely common in modern LLM-written JS (ubiquitous method
definitions); previously a ParserException.

Parser: in object_elem(), after the key token is consumed, detect a
following L_PAREN and emit a synthetic FN_EXPR node whose children
are [FN_DECL_ARGS, BLOCK] — no leading FUNCTION token. The element
tree becomes [IDENT, FN_EXPR] (plus a trailing COMMA when not the
last elem).

Interpreter: evalFnExpr now branches on node.getFirst().type ==

recognizes the shape by checking elem.get(1).type == FN_EXPR and
evaluates the method, binding it under the key.

Destructuring patterns never produce this shape, so the bindScope
path is unaffected.

Default session cookie SameSite=Lax, not Strict
Strict blocks the cookie on cross-site top-level navigations — which is
exactly what an OAuth callback is (the provider 302s the user from
workos.com back to our /signin?code=...). Under Strict, the browser drops
the cookie on that navigation and we lose the pre-redirect session state
(authType, CSRF state), leaving the callback with "Session expired. Please
try again."

Lax allows cookies on top-level navigations (links, form submits, redirects)
regardless of origin, but still blocks embedded requests (iframes, fetches,
image loads). That's the right default for session cookies used in OAuth
flows, and matches what Spring / Django / Rails default to.

Discovered when deploying studio to AWS and hitting the classic WorkOS
callback → "Session expired" failure.

   `match (0 == null) == false` failed because the lexer treated the

W3C: fix critical return-prefix bug, frame tests 16/16 pass

auto-prefix "return " for W3C compatibility.

navigation from 1/3 to 3/3, and frame from 5/16 to 16/16.

This eliminates two sources of allocation overhead:

   analysis and scalar replacement vs varargs array creation.

- Object[] allocations: 11.0GB → 6.9GB (-37%)
- Lambda allocations: 2.3GB → ~0GB (-99%)

- Throughput: ~7,000 → ~13,780 iterations (+97%)

fix: handle #(^expr) macro for array contains partial match
When using `match actual contains '#(^part)'` where actual is an array
and part is a partial object, the match should check if any element
in the array CONTAINS the partial object.

Previously, the macro would evaluate to CONTAINS type but then
actualContainsExpected() would use EQUALS for element comparison,
causing false negatives for partial matches.

The fix adds special handling in macroEqualsExpected() when:
- actual is a list
- evalResult (from macro) is a Map
- nestedType is CONTAINS or CONTAINS_ANY

In this case, iterate over elements and check if any matches.

Also includes:
- StepExecutor: only process embedded expressions for JSON literals

fix(knowledge): prevent duplicate RAGFlow docs on Ragflow-RAG re-slice
Previously, every save of slice config on a Ragflow-RAG knowledge base
uploaded a brand-new RAGFlow document and left the previous one as an
orphan, accumulating N copies per file. FileInfoV2.lastUuid already
stored the previous doc id on the Java side but was never forwarded to
Python, so RagflowRAGStrategy.split() unconditionally created new docs.

This PR wires lastUuid end-to-end and implements an atomic blue-green
upsert on the Python side: upload new -> parse -> fetch chunks -> delete
old. Any failure in upload, parse, fetch, or an empty-chunks response
rolls back the pending new doc and preserves the old doc, so the file
stays retrievable.

[C++] Give PersistentSubscriptionWrapperTest dedicated archive control ports (#2086)
PersistentSubscriptionWrapperTest used localhost:8010 / :8011 for its archive control request channels,
the same fixed ports as the archive system tests (aeron_archive_test / archiveTestW). When one of those
tests is killed by the CTest timeout (e.g. a replication test hanging on Windows), it can leave an orphaned
media driver holding the port. The next test to run, persistentSubscriptionTestW, then fails immediately
with "channel error - Address already in use: bind ... endpoint=localhost:8010" - a misleading second
failure that masks the actual culprit. Move this test to dedicated ports (8200/8201) that no other test
binary uses so a neighbouring test's timeout cannot cascade into it.

[Java] Lower Windows TestCluster startup-canvass timeout to fit @InterruptAfter budgets (#2085)
Setting the Windows cluster-test timeouts to the production defaults gave a 60s startup-canvass
timeout, but the per-test @InterruptAfter budgets (typically 30-40s) are sized for a much smaller
value. A test that restarts a node while only a bare quorum is present can never form a unanimous
candidate, so the restarting node must wait out the full startup-canvass deadline before it can
nominate itself. On Windows that 60s deadline exceeds the test budget, so such tests deterministically
hang to @InterruptAfter and fail (e.g. shouldRecoverWhenLeaderHasAppendedMoreThanFollower).

Keep the Windows timeouts larger than other platforms for slow-runner liveness headroom
(heartbeat 4s, startup-canvass 12s, termination 4s) but comfortably below the test budgets.

[Flink] Throttle Flink metric updates from source readers (#40610)
ReaderInvocationUtil pushed Beam metrics to Flink after every call to
Reader#start and Reader#advance. Each push builds the metric results of
all steps of the task and filters them down to one step. In a profiled
batch job this took 37.6% of the CPU of the read stage, more than
reading the records.

that, and whenever the reader has no data. Metrics are still recorded
on every call, and the metrics of the pipeline result, which come from
the Flink accumulator, are not affected.

Fix Python VarIntCoder OverflowError on uint64 values (#39047)
* [BEAM] Fix Python VarIntCoder OverflowError on uint64 values

The Cython write_var_int64/get_varint_size stream methods take a signed
int64_t parameter. A Python int in the unsigned 64-bit range [2**63,
2**64) -- a uint64 -- is converted to that signed parameter at the call
boundary and rejected with an OverflowError before the method body runs,
even though the body already operates on the unsigned bit pattern and the
VarInt wire encoding is well-defined.

Fold such values to the signed int64 with the identical bit pattern (and
thus identical VarInt encoding) before handing them to the stream. This
matches Java's signed VarIntCoder on the wire; decoding remains signed.
Values past 64 bits are left unchanged and still overflow downstream,
preserving the coder's documented 64-bit limit.

Adds test_varint_coder_uint64 covering no-overflow encoding, wire
equivalence to the signed twin, size estimation, signed decode, and the

[IcebergIO] Fix stale openWriters count in RecordWriterManager (#39157)
RecordWriterManager uses a Guava Cache with expireAfterAccess(1 min)
for writer eviction. However, Guava Cache eviction is lazy — expired
entries are only removed on subsequent access or explicit cleanUp().
The write() method checks `openWriters >= maxNumWriters` without first
calling cleanUp(), so expired writers remain in the cache and
openWriters stays stale.

With DEFAULT_MAX_WRITERS_PER_BUNDLE = 20 and more than 20 partitions,
this causes 100% false spill — every record for the 21st+ partition
is rejected as if the writer pool is full.

Add writers.cleanUp() before the capacity check to evict expired
entries and update openWriters accurately.

fix(python): Register all output pcollections of a transform rather than only ones that happened to be accessed in DoOutputsTuple (#37556)

outputs, but _pcolls is lazily populated — entries are only added when
accessed via __getitem__. This caused unaccessed outputs (e.g. the main
output) to be missing from the composite's registered outputs in the
pipeline proto. Fix by iterating over all declared tags (_main_tag + _tags)
and accessing each via __getitem__ to ensure lazy creation.

Show "Korean" instead of "Ko" in translators list (#8706)
### Description

The translators list in `Settings → About` shows `Ko` for the Korean
translation, while every other row shows a full language name.
`scripts/createContributors.py` derives the name with
`pycountry.languages.lookup("ko").name`, and ISO 639-3 contains a
language literally named "Ko", which `lookup()` can match ahead of
Korean's `alpha_2` code. `ANDROID_LANG_FIXES` already exists for this
class of problem, so this adds `"ko": "Korean"` there and applies the
resulting value to the two generated files. I could not run the script
to confirm the `pycountry` behaviour, so the diagnosis is based on
reading the code; the wrong value in the generated files is reproducible
regardless.

Closes: #8705

Fix intermittent page title reset on navigation (#27476)
* Fix intermittent page title reset on navigation

`DocumentTitle` treated `document.title` as an accumulator it
read-modify-wrote, with no notion of which instance owned the value:

  document.title = `${document.title} - ${title}`;   // append
  return () => { document.title = productName; };    // clobber all

That is only correct if at most one instance is mounted at a time and
the outgoing cleanup always runs before the incoming effect. React
guarantees neither. `AppRouter` enables `v7_startTransition`, so route
changes are concurrent updates and the incoming page can mount before
the outgoing one unmounts. The late cleanup then wiped a title it no
longer owned, leaving the bare product name.

Derive the title from `productName` instead of the current value, and
guard the reset with an ownership token so a stale cleanup cannot
clobber a title another instance has taken over. The token is compared
by identity rather than by s

Replace copied Netty frame decoders with subclasses (#27780)
LenientDelimiterBasedFrameDecoder and LenientLineBasedFrameDecoder were
copied from Netty 4.1.19 in 2018 and missed upstream fixes since then:
- Quadratic scanning for non-line delimiters (GHSA-5h6f-wp3f-6hmv),
  affecting GELF TCP which uses the null delimiter by default.
- Stale scan offset while discarding a too long line (netty/netty#8257),
  which dropped the following lines or failed with an
  IndexOutOfBoundsException.

The only Graylog addition was emitting the remaining bytes as the last
frame when the channel is closed. Implement that in decodeLast() on top
of Netty's DelimiterBasedFrameDecoder and LineBasedFrameDecoder, so we
get upstream fixes with Netty updates.

DelimiterBasedFrameDecoder only delegates line delimiters to
LineBasedFrameDecoder if it isn't subclassed. Do the delegation in
LenientDelimiterBasedFrameDecoder to keep the line based behavior and
performance for line delimited TCP inputs and HTTP bulk

ESLint 9's flat config system calls `structuredClone()` internally in

Fix MCP ping returning -32603 instead of an empty result (#27123)
* Fix MCP ping returning -32603 instead of an empty result

McpService.handle() returns Optional.empty() for the ping utility. In
McpRestResource.post(), result.orElse(null) then passed null as both the
result and the error to the McpSchema.JSONRPCResponse constructor, whose SDK
validation requires exactly one of the two to be non-null. The resulting
IllegalArgumentException was caught by the generic handler and returned as
HTTP 500 / JSON-RPC -32603 "MCP responses MUST either have a result or error".

Substitute an empty map when handle() yields no result body, so ping returns
the spec-required "result": {}. An empty map is used because the SDK has no
empty McpSchema.Result type, Map.of() serialises reliably to {} under
Graylog's JAX-RS ObjectMapper, and it matches what the MCP Java SDK's own
server returns for ping.

Fixes #27066

Degrade gracefully when OSHI/JNA native load fails on noexec data dir (#26608)
* Degrade gracefully when OSHI/JNA native load fails on noexec data dir

The node CPU-load metric (NodeMetricPeriodical, new in 7.1.0) eagerly
built a CpuLoadGauge in a field initializer, which touched OSHI native
code in its own field initializer. Because the periodical is an
eagerly-instantiated @Singleton, this forced OSHI/JNA to unpack and
dlopen its native library during Guice injector creation. On hosts
where the Graylog data directory is on a noexec-mounted filesystem the
kernel refuses to map the library, raising an UnsatisfiedLinkError that
aborted startup entirely.

CpuLoadGauge now initializes lazily and guards native access with a
try/catch on Throwable (LinkageErrors are Errors, not Exceptions),
logging a single warning that points at the likely noexec cause and the
jna.tmpdir remedy, then disabling the metric. The metric being
unavailable no longer prevents the node from starting.

Preload Material Symbols icon font to avoid font-display fallback (#26609)
The icon `@font-face` uses `font-display: block`, and the font is only fetched
lazily when the first icon paints. In slow/cold environments (e.g. headless
e2e), that fetch can miss the block window and icons fall back to their ligature
source text ("search", ...) instead of the glyph.

Emit a real `<link rel="preload" as="font" crossorigin>` from the early-loading
`preload` entry (runs before `app.js`) so the font fetch starts up front and is
ready by the time icons render. The webpack-resolved URL matches the `@font-face`
`src`, so the preload is reused rather than double-fetched.

Fix JIT emulator re-executing delay slots when a branch falls through
The p-code of an instruction with a delay slot already includes the p-code
of its delay-slotted instruction(s). DefaultPcodeThread accounts for this
by advancing the counter by InstructionDecoder#getLastLengthWithDelays(),
but the JIT's DecoderExecutor#getAdvancedAddress() used
instruction.getMaxAddress().next(). When a delay-slotted branch was not
taken, the JIT therefore fell through to the delay slot address and
executed the delay-slotted instruction a second time.

Record the length including delay slots when the decoder decodes an
instruction, and use it to compute the fall-through address.

Add MIPS tests for a taken and a not-taken delay-slotted branch to
AbstractPcodeEmulatorTest, so both the plain and JIT emulators run them.
Without the fix, JitPcodeEmulatorTest#testDelaySlotBranchNotTaken fails
with "expected:<1> but was:<2>".

Issue #5214: Recover compiler for minidump-loaded PE programs
The Dump File loader sets the executable format to "Portable Executable
(PE)" but never runs compiler detection, so program.getCompiler() stays
"unknown" for minidump-loaded programs. The Microsoft PE analyzers (RTTI,
TEB, exception handling) are gated by PEUtil.isVisualStudioOrClangPe(),
which also requires a Visual Studio / Clang compiler, so they are never
offered for a dumped process even when it is a Visual Studio / Clang PE.

Detect the compiler of the dumped main executable image (module 0) in
Minidump.analyze() and record it on the program, reusing the existing
PeLoader.CompilerOpinion. Only the main module is examined so the many
Microsoft-compiled system DLLs present in a dump do not misidentify the
program's compiler; non-Microsoft main modules (e.g. GCC) remain correctly
identified and excluded. Parsing failures are ignored, leaving the
compiler unset as before.

Avoid scanning the whole layer index for every entry
IndexedLayers.getLayer() walked every entry of layers.idx for each jar
entry being extracted, making extraction O(entries x index size). The
dependency entries are listed first while the application classes are
covered by a single directory entry near the end, so the most numerous
entries consistently scanned the longest.

directory candidates in a separate map that preserves index order. A
file name is then resolved with a single map lookup and only the

2.5ms). With 4,173 entries it goes from 1,019,857 to 11,896 (5.4ms to

* ESQL: add cross-driver global TopN merge for timestamp opt

Part 2 of the specialized SORT @timestamp DESC, LIMIT N optimization
series (split from prototype #156520, following Part 1 #157717).

Adds SharedGlobalTopK: a shared, lock-protected global top-K heap
that aggregates per-driver local heaps and publishes a competitive
@timestamp bound to SharedMinCompetitive as soon as the global heap
reaches LIMIT rows, regardless of how many rows any single driver has
seen. This fires a tighter bound than per-driver publishing alone,
which requires one driver to accumulate LIMIT rows first.

Key design points:
- Merge runs every batch_pages pages (default 1) to amortize lock
  contention without sacrificing bound quality.
- Per-driver direct publish in updateMinCompetitive() is suppressed
  when global merge is active so the two paths do not conflict.
- A final merge is performed in finish() to ensure the global heap

ESQL: release external-Parquet page decompress buffers per page, not per row group (#153038)
* ESQL: release external-Parquet page decompress buffers per page, not per row group

PrefetchedPageReader parked every decompressed page's direct Arrow buffer for
the whole row-group lifetime, releasing only at close(). The live decompressed
working set per (column, reader) was O(uncompressed column chunk) rather than
O(one page); multiplied across projected columns and concurrent read streams it
climbed until the OS OOM-killer took the node, invisible to every heap-only
circuit breaker.

readPage() now releases the previous page's decompress-output buffer(s) before
decompressing the next, uniformly for the V1, V2 and uncompressed short-circuit
paths, bounding the live working set to O(one page). close() still releases the
tail page, so the reader's external contract is unchanged. Safe because
parquet-mr consumes pages strictly sequentially through PageColumnReader:
loadNextPage finishes decod

AI requests to a self-hosted OpenAI-compatible server over plaintext http://
(vLLM, Ollama, LM Studio, ...) arrive at the server with no body, so the
endpoint rejects them or the request hangs. vLLM/FastAPI answers POST
/v1/responses with:

  1 validation error:
  {'type': 'missing', 'loc': ('body',), 'msg': 'Field required', 'input': None}

unsupported upgrade and stop parsing the request, handing the application an
empty body. HTTPS endpoints negotiate via ALPN and never send those headers,
which is why only self-hosted plaintext endpoints are affected.

On Greenplum 7 and Cloudberry, external tables are implemented on top

provided by that extension, and the legacy pg_class.relstorage column

GreenplumTableCache.prepareLookupStatement already resolves

GreenplumExternalTable instances for relkind 'r' and 'p'. As a result,
on Cloudberry connections external tables appeared under FOREIGN TABLES

Fix native tool host/port extraction for URL-based connections (#40534)
When a database connection uses URL configuration type instead of manual
field-based configuration, the native tool (mysqldump, pg_dump, etc.)
fails to extract the host and port from the connection URL. This results
in an empty --host= parameter being passed to the native tool, causing
connection failures.

Three issues are fixed:
1. The URI fallback parser was only used when sampleUrl was null, but
   not when extractConfigurationFromUrl failed to match the URL pattern.
   Now the URI fallback is always attempted when hostname is empty.
2. An empty --host= parameter was always appended even when hostname
   could not be determined. Now --host= is only added when hostname
   is non-empty.
3. URI.getPort() returns -1 when no port is specified. The old code
   used String.valueOf() which produced "-1" and passed it as --port=-1.
   Now the port value is only used when it is a positive integer.

Fix misleading NPE when request parameter is not Serializable (#16299)
* Fix misleading NPE when request parameter is not Serializable

When a Dubbo service is called with non-serializable parameters, the
invocation deserialization fails silently and `path` becomes null. This
null path is then passed to GroupServiceKeyCache which uses a
ConcurrentHashMap that does not accept null keys, resulting in a
confusing NullPointerException.

Added a null check for `path` in DubboProtocol.getInvoker() to throw
a clear RemotingException with a meaningful message pointing users to
the actual cause (non-serializable parameters).

Fixes #16293
