* Replace cached gzip theme resources atomically

Concurrent first requests for a theme resource each gzip it to a temp
file and move it over the cached copy. Without ATOMIC_MOVE the JDK
replaces an existing target by deleting it and then renaming, so a
request opening the file in between gets FileNotFoundException (and on
JDK 17 a second mover's own delete can fail with NoSuchFileException).
getEncodedStream then returns null and the resource is answered with
404.

Publish the cache file only by an ATOMIC_MOVE of the completed temp
file, which is in the target's directory, so a cached file that exists
is always complete. On POSIX this is a rename(2) that replaces the
target in one step; on Windows it is a MoveFileEx replace, which fails
while another request has the target open. Racing requests all write
the same content, so if the move fails and the target exists, serve
that target. If the move fails and there is no target, serv

Use deterministic ROUND time-claim strategy in OID4VCI conformance realm
The Oid4VciNonHaipTestSuite conformance job was intermittently failing on
the oid4vci-1_0-issuer-happy-flow-multiple-clients module, whose
VCIEnsureCredentialTimeClaimsNotLinkable check (RFC 9901 10.1) occasionally
flagged the iat claim as linkable. The realm used the RANDOMIZE time-claim
strategy, which is probabilistic: the two independent random offsets applied
to the same-dataset credentials sometimes coincide, leaving an iat delta that
matches the real inter-issuance gap and tripping the check.

Switch the conformance realm to the deterministic ROUND strategy with a
MINUTE unit. Rounding quantizes iat to unit boundaries so the delta between
two credentials issued seconds apart is either 0 or a full unit, never
approximately the real gap. MINUTE is the coarsest usable unit here: exp is
computed from the already-normalized iat and the scopes use a 300s (5 min)
expiry, so MINUTE keeps exp exactly 300s after iat,

Treat blank repeat fields as unset in time-based policies
The admin console persists empty strings for unused repeat fields of a
time policy (month, dayMonth, hour, ...). TimePolicyProvider only checked
these values for null before parsing them, so evaluating any permission
that referenced such a policy failed with a NumberFormatException.

Blank or whitespace-only start values are now ignored, and a blank end
value falls back to an exact match on the start value, consistent with
the existing nbf/noa handling.

Closes #53456

Treat DATA frames on reserved HTTP/2 streams as a connection error (#17868)
Motivation:
A DATA frame on a stream in the RESERVED_REMOTE state (on a client that
received a PUSH_PROMISE) or RESERVED_LOCAL state (on a server that sent
one) caused an UnsupportedOperationException from

they still use the reduced flow control state, but

UnsupportedOperationException was passed to exceptionCaught. Even
without that, the decoder would only have raised a stream error, while
RFC 9113, section 5.1 requires a connection error of type PROTOCOL_ERROR
for DATA frames on idle or reserved streams.

Don't count STOMP headers again when the header block is replayed (#17664)
Motivation:

`StompSubframeDecoder` is a `ReplayingDecoder`. When the header block of
a frame is not complete, the next read parses the command and all
headers again from the checkpoint. The counter that enforces
`maxNumHeaders` (`HeaderParser.numHeaders`, added in #17063) is only
reset by the empty line that ends the headers. So every replay adds the
headers that were already counted.

As a result, whether a valid frame is rejected with "maximum number of
headers exceeded" depends on how it is split into reads. After the
rejection, the decoder stays in `BAD_FRAME`. With the default limit of
128:

| Frame | Reads | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 15 headers | sent byte by byte, or one line at a time from a terminal
| rejected |
| 40 headers | 32-byte reads | rejected |
| 128 headers | 2 reads | rejected |
| 90 headers | one read | accepted |

KAFKA-20765: Fix OffsetFetch stale-epoch retry spinning in dedup loop (#22747)
Fixes [KAFKA-20765](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/KAFKA-20765).

## The issue

In the async consumer (`AsyncKafkaConsumer`), when an in-flight
OffsetFetch fails with `STALE_MEMBER_EPOCH` and a refreshed member epoch
is already known, `CommitRequestManager` correctly classifies the error
as retriable — but the retry can enter a tight, non-progressing loop
instead of being re-sent:

1. Two callers fetch committed offsets for the same partitions. The
second request is deduplicated by
`PendingRequests.addOffsetFetchRequest` and *chained* onto the first
(in-flight) one.
2. The in-flight request fails with `STALE_MEMBER_EPOCH` (e.g. another
member joined and the coordinator bumped the group epoch while the
request was in flight — routine under the KIP-1071 streams protocol

KAFKA-20723: Resolve DLQ copy records per produce round. (#22919)
* ShareGroupDLQStateManager previously resolved a DLQ record parameter's
entire archived offset range once, eagerly, before the handler was even
enqueued to send - capping total copyable content at roughly one
message's worth (regardless of how many produce requests the range
needed) and delaying the first produce request until the whole range,
including any remote-tiered reads, had been read.

now fetches only the window starting at nextOffsetToSend, with a fresh

next round before rejoining the coalescing node map. This lets a large
range recover real content across every round it needs, and lets the
first produce request go out as soon as its own round resolves.

this: an uncaught exception from one handler's

KAFKA-20723: Bound decompression memory in ShareGroupDLQRecordFetcher (#22905)
### What

A compressed source record could decompress to far more data than its
on-wire size suggests, since the previous implementation fully
materialized a compressed batch via `DefaultRecordBatch.iterator()` and
allocated per-record buffers based on an unchecked, attacker-controlled
length.

### How
Compressed v2 batches are now decompressed into a size-capped
buffer before any record is parsed, so even a single oversized record
can't force a large allocation; the cap is derived from the DLQ topic's
own `max.message.bytes` rather than an arbitrary constant. Uncompressed
batches are left uncapped (no expansion risk), and fetch()/resume() now
catch Throwable so an OOM can't escape uncontained.

### Testing
Added new unit tests in `ShareGroupDLQRecordFetcherTest` and integ tests
in `ShareConsumerDLQTest`.

KAFKA-20760: Stage position updates in InMemorySessionStore transaction buffer (#22745)
`InMemorySessionStore`, when transactional, did not correctly track its
`Position` across the transaction boundary, breaking interactive-query
position consistency in two ways. The root cause is the same as the
parallel fix for `InMemoryKeyValueStore`.

**Staging.** `put` called `StoreQueryUtils.updatePosition` directly on
the store's committed `Position` on every write, bypassing the
transaction boundary, so IQv2 position-bound queries could observe
position advances corresponding to records not yet visible. Position
updates are now staged into a `pendingPosition` field on
`InMemorySessionTransactionBuffer` under the existing `snapshotLock`,
and merged into the committed position at commit time via
`mergePendingPositionInto`. `discardPendingBatch` resets the pending
position on abort. Under READ_UNCOMMITTED, `query` merges the pending
deltas so staged writes remain visible, mirroring `RocksDBStore`

KAFKA-20434: Consumer group does not recompute assignment when static members rejoin with different assignor (#22036)
When all static members of a consumer group using the consumer protocol
leave and rejoin with a different server-side assignor, the group does
not recompute the target assignment. The `bumpGroupEpoch` flag only
considers changes to subscribed topic names and regex but not the
preferred server assignor.

This patch adds a `hasPreferredServerAssignorChanged` check that
compares the effective preferred assignor (falling back to the default
when no member has an explicit preference) before and after the member
update. The group epoch is bumped when the effective preferred assignor
changes, which only happens once a majority of members has switched.

addresses the review feedback there):

1. ServerMemberManager.hasMember(String): the IP-only fallback used a substring

The lost wake-up is decide() returning null on a workflow-lock miss: the
completion-event callers (updateTask, AsyncSystemTaskExecutor) ignore that
null, so the next task is never scheduled and the workflow parks on its

fix(sweeper): re-queue on lock miss to eliminate multi-minute workflow pauses
The active WorkflowSweeper.sweep() bare-returned when it couldn't acquire the
workflow lock, doing nothing to advance or reschedule the workflow. A
lock-contended workflow (e.g. at a JOIN boundary) then fell back to its
decider-queue entry, which a polled task postpones out to
responseTimeoutSeconds via ExecutionService.adjustDeciderQueuePostpone().
With responseTimeoutSeconds=600 this surfaces as an intermittent ~10-minute
pause per contended transition (reported on 3.30.2 with Spanner persistence
and Redis queue/locks).

Fix: on a lock miss, re-queue the workflow to the decider queue with a bounded
backoff (lockLeaseTime/2, capped by maxPostponeDurationSeconds) so it is
retried in seconds instead of parking. The identical backoff math previously
inlined in the decide()==null path is factored into a shared
lockContentionBackoffSeconds() helper. The existing "Couldn't acquire lock to
sweep workflow" error log

writes one marked-content sequence per piece. It cannot nest one sequence in
another, so when two pieces of one string overlapped, one was written and
the other's MCID pointed at nothing. On a scan's OCR layer the pieces of one
string came as [1,2) and then [0,5), each in its own addMcidChildren call,
so the existing merge of adjacent pieces never saw them together.

already marks, the earlier piece is now widened to cover both, and no MCID
is added for the later one. Pieces of two different elements are left as
they are.

without content 8 -> 1, and the scanned D2 now passes tag-audit. Tagged

node is empty or space-only. getHeadersOrFootersIntervals dereferenced it
straight away, so such a node raised NullPointerException out of

fix(core): wrap path construction in its marked-content sequence
A path is built by construction operators (re/m/l/c/v/y/h) and realised
by a paint operator. Only the paint operator reached
processContentOperator, so BDC/EMC wrapped the paint alone and every
preceding construction operator stayed outside it. The shape was drawn
but belonged to no marked-content sequence, leaving it unreachable from
the structure tree.

Charts are the visible casualty: bars, axes and gridlines are almost
entirely construction operators, so a chart the AI had detected as a
figure reached the tagged PDF with its geometry untagged.

Buffer construction operators and emit them inside the span with their
paint operator. A path consumed by a clip (W/W*) or discarded (n) draws
nothing, so it is flushed untagged.

Also routes B and B* (fill-then-stroke) to processContentOperator. They
were absent from the paint list, so those paints were never wrapped;
left out, they would now also carry the buffered path back

fix: temporarily disable TOC detection until it is complete
Objective: PDF/UA-2 validation fails on documents where a table of contents
is detected. The detected TOC cannot become a conformant structure: each entry
must point at the section it references, but the pipeline never resolves that
target, so the tagged output has no valid reference and fails clause 8.2.5.8.1.
On top of that the detector is triggered too eagerly (any line ending in a
number looks like a TOC entry), so it can even restructure ordinary body text.

Approach: Turn the feature off at its single call site until it is finished,
rather than shipping a half-working table of contents. A partial TOC is worse
than none — an entry that points nowhere (or to the wrong place) sends a screen
reader astray, and the false positives corrupt normal content. Detection is
only commented out (the processor stays in the tree) so re-enabling is a
one-line change once entry-target resolution and detection precision are done.

fix: pass headless JVM flags so macOS does not show Dock icon
Objective: On macOS, every CLI run pops a Java icon in the Dock and
steals focus from the active window — so any batch or repeated PDF
conversion turns into a flickering, focus-thrashing experience.

Approach: Pass -Djava.awt.headless=true and -Dapple.awt.UIElement=true
as JVM args ahead of -jar at every spawn site (Node wrapper, Python
wrapper, scripts/run-cli.sh, npm export-options). The CLI never opens
a UI — it only manipulates BufferedImages and renders PDFBox pages off
screen — so headless is safe everywhere. apple.awt.UIElement is the
macOS-specific flag the launcher reads to skip Dock registration; it
is harmless on other OSes.

Evidence: Ran the built jar and the Node wrapper against a sample PDF
on macOS.

Before: every invocation surfaced a Java Dock icon and stole focus.
After (java -D... -jar):    PDF processed, JSON written, no Dock icon.
After (Node convert() API): variant resolved successfully, no Dock icon.

fix(hybrid): auto-chunk large PDFs to prevent backend hang on 100+ page documents
Objective: When processing large scanned PDFs (100+ pages) in hybrid mode,
the backend hangs indefinitely. The server stays alive but never returns a
response, forcing users to manually split PDFs into ~30-page chunks.

Approach: Automatically split backend-routed pages into 50-page chunks in
the Java client — the server already supports page_ranges, so no server
change is needed. 50 pages was chosen based on empirical testing: it
matches 30-page chunks in total time while requiring fewer requests. The
AI model is loaded once at server startup (singleton), so there is no
per-request model loading overhead from chunking.

   NPE and skipped the heading entirely, leaving it with default level 0

fix: suppress LineArtChunk from JSON output (#244)
LineArtChunk (verapdf vector graphics) was serialized as type="image"
via LineArtSerializer, misleading RAG consumers who expected a source
key that was never written.

Remove LineArtSerializer and add explicit instanceof guards in all
five JSON output sites that iterate IObject children via writePOJO:
JsonWriter, TableSerializer (textBlock path), TableCellSerializer,
HeaderFooterSerializer, and ListItemSerializer.

TableBorderProcessor can place LineArtChunk into cell contents when
chunk-cell overlap is ≤ 90%, so the nested serializer guards are
necessary beyond the top-level JsonWriter filter.

Markdown/HTML output already silently dropped LineArtChunk via their
isSupportedContent allowlist; JSON now behaves consistently.

fix: handle Docling PARTIAL_SUCCESS and fallback failed pages to Java (#216)
Fixes #215

When Docling encounters malformed Unicode in a PDF's font encoding, it
raises "Invalid code point" and skips affected pages, returning
PARTIAL_SUCCESS. The hybrid server previously ignored this status,
always reporting "success" — causing the Java client to silently drop
failed pages.

Python (hybrid_server.py):
- New `build_conversion_response()` detects failed pages by comparing
  expected vs present page numbers in the output
- Reports `status`, `errors`, and `failed_pages` in the response
- Uses ConversionStatus enum for status comparison in convert_file

Java:
- HybridResponse: added immutable `failedPages` field with
  backward-compatible constructors
- DoclingFastServerClient: parses `partial_success` status and
  `failed_pages` array with defensive handling of malformed values
- HybridDocumentProcessor: falls back to Java processing for failed
  pages, respecting the `fallbackToJava` config

fix: prevent stack trace exposure in hybrid server error response
Return a generic error message instead of exception type and details

fix(executions): worker task resubmission on a terminated execution
A kill only reaches workers that are still alive, so the WorkerTaskRunning
entry of a dead worker outlives the execution it belongs to. When the
liveness coordinator swept it after the termination grace period it
re-emitted the job unconditionally, giving a KILLED execution a new
RESUBMITTED attempt that ran the task with its real side effects.

resubmitWorkerTask now reads the execution before re-emitting and drops the
running entry instead when the execution is terminal or KILLING. RUNNING and
PAUSED executions keep worker-crash recovery unchanged.

fix(flows): only suggest reachable task ids after `outputs.` (#20718)
Every task id in the flow was offered wherever the cursor was, so an
`errors` task showed up inside `tasks`, where its output can never exist,
and a later sibling showed up in an earlier one. Pebble renders with
strict variables, so accepting either suggestion fails the task at run

an earlier root section (tasks < errors < finally < afterExecution), or
the same section and a block closed before the current one starts, which
also drops the enclosing flowable. Without a resolvable cursor task
(no-code expression inputs) the list stays unscoped. Parallel and Dag
siblings are still suggested; left as a known gap.

fix(tasks): docker image pull for references with a digest (#19667)
A containerImage carrying a digest (`name:tag@sha256:...` or `name@sha256:...`)
failed with `Status 400: {"message":"invalid reference format"}`, because
`getImageNameWithoutTag` cut the reference at its last `:` — which, for a digest
reference, is the one inside the digest itself. The pull then went out as
`fromImage=cytopia/ansible:2.20-tools@sha256&tag=latest`.

Split the digest off before the tag and pass it as the tag, which is what
`/images/create` expects for a digest pull. When the part after `@` carries no
colon it is left in place so the daemon still rejects the reference, rather than
an empty tag pulling every tag in the repository or a bare one pulling an
unrelated image. The parsing moves next to `registryUrlFromImage` in
DockerService so it can be unit tested.

Closes https://github.com/kestra-io/kestra/issues/15694.

Micronaut's ErrorController produced an identical JsonError body/status for a
genuinely-missing resource (NotFoundException) and for an unmatched route,
making it impossible for a client to tell a real not-found apart from a route

fix(core): keep explicit nulls nested in task outputs (#18938)
* fix(core): keep explicit nulls nested in task outputs

An explicit null nested inside a task output (a null in a Map or List, not a
top-level bean property) was turned into an absent key, so a downstream
expression like `{{ outputs.produce.records[0].b }}` failed with
"Unable to find 'b'" instead of rendering an empty value.

`Output.toMap()` used the JSON mapper configured with the single-argument
`setDefaultPropertyInclusion(NON_NULL)`, which drops null map entries and
collection elements at every depth. A dedicated mapper separates the two
inclusion settings (NON_NULL value, ALWAYS content) and is used only by
`Output.toMap()`, so every output producer is covered at once without touching
flow YAML, API payloads or revision diffs.

Tests cover both null-inclusion cases on the memory runner, the full round-trip
through the output store on H2, MySQL and Postgres, and both JacksonMapper
overloads.

fix(flows): load a row's execution chart once it nears the viewport (#18935)
Closes https://github.com/kestra-io/kestra/issues/18405.

The Execution statistics column renders one TimeSeries per row, and each one
asked the backend for its own preview on mount, so opening Flows fired one
`dashboards/charts/preview` request per listed flow regardless of what the user

declared non-recyclable: unmounting a chart that scrolled away would re-issue
the request on the way back, which is what this is saving.

Measured on a running instance with 15 flows listed: 15 requests on arrival
before, 9 after, reaching 15 again only once the table is scrolled to the
bottom, so no chart is lost.

A webhook read the body of every call into the execution: a binary one
base64-encoded onto `trigger.body`, inflated by a third, held in memory
in full. That is right for the JSON payload a webhook usually receives,

feat(triggers): store webhook file parts in the internal storage
A `multipart/form-data` webhook request carried the content of its file
parts base64-encoded on `trigger.parts[].content`, so a file travelled
through the execution record, inflated by a third, after being read into
memory in full.

The content of a file part is now streamed into Kestra's internal storage
as it is received, and the part carries its URI on `trigger.parts[].uri`.
Nothing about the file reaches the execution but its metadata, and a file
of any size is handled without ever being held in memory.

Storing a file before the execution exists means knowing its identifier
first, so the webhook routes mint it up front and hand it down through
`WebhookContext`, as trigger evaluation already does for polling
triggers. The parts are stored under that execution and purged with it;
a call that creates no execution - conditions not met, or inputs that
fail to render - deletes what it stored.

fix(tasks): skip Docker VOLUME output download when nothing is declared (#17311)
The Docker task runner creates a files volume as soon as a task uploads
input files, enables an output directory or declares output files
(`needVolume`). The output download at the end of the run was gated on
that same `needVolume` flag, so a task that merely uploaded `inputFiles`
(and declared no output) still streamed its whole working directory back
over the Docker socket via `copyArchiveFromContainerCmd`.

On large working directories (e.g. a pip venv built in place) this
pointless transfer fails with `TruncatedChunkException`.

Restrict `downloadOutputFiles` to the cases where an output was actually
requested (`outputFiles` or the deprecated `outputDir`), while still
creating the volume for the input-file upload.

feat(cli): print UI URL as the last line once the server is fully ready
Adds a distinctive, prefix-free banner with the Kestra UI URL that reliably
appears as the *last* line of the terminal output once startup is complete:

    ✅ Kestra is ready! Open the UI at: http://localhost:8080

A running server boots several services on staggered timers (executor, worker,
scheduler, indexer, controller) plus a liveness coordinator that elects a
leader and kicks off trigger scheduling a few seconds after the others report
RUNNING. Printing the banner synchronously leaves it buried in that async log
burst. ReadinessBanner instead attaches a tiny logback appender that tracks the
timestamp of every log event and prints only after the log stream has been
quiet for a short window — data-driven rather than a fixed sleep, with a safety
cap so it never blocks startup.

fix(tasks): PurgeLogs should match namespace as a prefix
`PurgeLogs` (and any caller of the log repository's bulk `deleteByQuery`)
filtered the namespace with an exact equality, while `PurgeExecutions`
matches the namespace and all its descendants, and the `PurgeLogs.namespace`
property is documented as a prefix.

As a result, a purge flow iterating over parent namespaces (e.g. `automation`)
would delete the matching executions but never the associated logs, since all
logs live in child namespaces (`automation.*`). The logs table kept growing
despite a daily purge.

Align the log delete condition with `PurgeExecutions`: when no `flowId` is
provided, match the namespace itself and its descendants
(`namespace = X OR namespace LIKE 'X.%'`); when a `flowId` is provided, keep
the exact-namespace match.

Page a leased text value without holding or re-copying it
Reading a leased value kept every byte produced so far and copied all of it
again on each slice, so paging cost quadratic time and up to the whole
value on the heap, outside the snapshot memory budget and disk limits that
exist to bound exactly that. The reader now keeps a live window: a slice
copies only the bytes it returns, the handed out prefix is dropped by
moving an index, and the buffer is compacted and grown instead of being
re-copied. A caller that asks for an offset already dropped reads the
value again from its start, which costs a pass over the cursor instead of
the heap.

Measured on a 1 MiB page size: 16/32/64/128 MiB went from 35/57/109/369 ms
to 11/16/45/42 ms, and paging a 256 MiB leased value now completes in a
64 MB heap where the previous reader failed with "Java heap space".

path, so a throwing stmt.close() no longer skips onStatementCl

fix(redis): null-safe value comparison when updating string keys
Updating a Redis string key threw NullPointerException in

because the value comparison called equals directly on it. A null new

With disallowAdditionalPropertiesIfNotPresent=false, an allOf child of a
discriminated oneOf/anyOf parent was tagged x-inherits-additional-properties

[java] fix: okhttp-gson additionalProperties field makes every allOf child undeserializable (#24895)
* [java] fix: the okhttp-gson additionalProperties bag breaks every allOf child

With disallowAdditionalPropertiesIfNotPresent=false every model declares
private Map<String, Object> additionalProperties - so an allOf child
declares the field twice, once itself and once inherited, and gson refuses
the class before the model's own TypeAdapterFactory can run:

    IllegalArgumentException: Class Child declares multiple JSON fields
    named 'additionalProperties'

Every allOf child model is undeserializable (and unserializable). Mark the
field transient: the custom TypeAdapterFactory already reads and writes the
bag explicitly around the reflective delegate - on write it even removes
the additionalProperties key the delegate emitted - so hiding it from
gson's reflection changes nothing for flat models and unbreaks the children.

does not know about.

fix(ruby): JSON-encode query params with content:application/json (#24126)
* fix(ruby): JSON-encode query params with content:application/json

Parameters declared with `content: { "application/json": ... }` must be
serialized as JSON strings per the OpenAPI 3 spec. The core model field
`queryIsJsonMimeType` was already set correctly by DefaultCodegen; the Ruby
template was simply not using it, causing raw Ruby object representations to
be sent instead of JSON.

Adds `{{#queryIsJsonMimeType}}...to_json{{/queryIsJsonMimeType}}` branches to
api.mustache for both required and optional query params, updates the three
ruby echo_api samples accordingly, and adds a RubyClientCodegenTest to assert
the flag is set on content:application/json parameters.

Fixes: #2519 (partially — same root cause, jaxrs-cxf generator)
Related: #6367, #21934 (same bug in TypeScript generators)

* fix(kotlin-spring): preserve 'default' response code in postProcessOperationsWithModels

When an OpenAPI spec defines a 'default' response (no specific status code),
the codegen internally represents it as code '0'. The existing logic
unconditionally mapped '0' -> '200', causing generated @ApiResponse annotations
to incorrectly use responseCode = "200" instead of responseCode = "default".

Fix: check resp.isDefault before mapping; only fall back to '200' for
non-default zero-coded responses.

Fixes #17445

[POWERSHELL] fix: single-quote DTO property names to prevent $-variable interpolation (#23624)
* [POWERSHELL] fix: single-quote DTO property names to prevent $-variable interpolation

PowerShell treats `$` inside double-quoted strings as the sigil for variable
interpolation, so `"$foo" = ${Foo}` inside a hash literal becomes `<value-of-$foo> = <value-of-Foo>`.
When an OpenAPI property name starts with (or contains) `$` — e.g. `$type` from
C# polymorphic payloads or `$ref` / `$schema` from JSON Schema — the generated
Initialize- and ConvertFrom- commandlets emit invalid PSCustomObject hash keys
and empty regex patterns, breaking DTO (de)serialization.

Swap all user-property-name emissions in `model_simple.mustache` from
double-quoted to single-quoted literals so baseName is preserved verbatim:

- `$PSO = [PSCustomObject]@{ '<baseName>' = ${<name>} }` (3 sites)
- `$AllProperties = ('<baseName>', ...)` (1 site)
- `-match '<baseName>'` and `.Properties['<baseName>']` (4 sites)

fix(java/feign): handle binary response types in ApiResponseDecoder (#22939)
* fix(java/feign): handle binary response types in ApiResponseDecoder

The Feign library's ApiResponseDecoder routes all responses through
JacksonDecoder, including binary ones (File, byte[], InputStream).
This causes JsonParseException when an endpoint returns non-JSON
content (e.g. PDF, ZIP, images).

Add binary type detection and handling before delegating to
JacksonDecoder. This applies to both direct return types and
ApiResponse<T> wrappers.

Consistent with the native library fix in #21346.

Closes #2486

Keep ANSI colours in the live console after a pause in output (#27424)
* Keep console annotator state across empty progressive log chunks

The streaming progressiveHtml response only includes consoleAnnotator
in its metadata when there is new text to render. When a poll returns
no new output, the client overwrote its stored state with undefined and
stopped sending X-ConsoleAnnotator, so every later chunk was rendered by
a fresh annotator: AnsiColor escapes appeared raw and Timestamper
formatting was lost until the page was reloaded.
